title: Diagram-as-Code for Cloud Architecture: Provider Node Hierarchies, Context Canvases, Fan-Out Grouping, Nested Clusters, and Typed Edge Protocols
author: Zaira Hira (freeCodeCamp.org, 2026; synthesized by Brain Harness)

source.title: How to Create System Design Diagrams using Python

claims.assertion: Architecture diagrams must be declared as code in version control rather than manually drawn in canvas tools, eliminating documentation drift and enabling automated CI/CD artifact generation.

A node object represents one discrete architectural component defined by a 3-part hierarchy: provider (e.g. aws, gcp, azure, k8s, onprem), resource_type (e.g. compute, database, network), and component name.
claims.source: Zaira Hira: 'What is Diagrams?' & 'Your First Diagram' (2026)

claims.assertion: Data flow directionality is represented via operator overloading: >> for forward/downstream flow, << for reverse/upstream flow, and - for undirected or symmetric peering/replication.
claims.source: Zaira Hira: 'How to Connect Nodes and Data Flow' (2026)

claims.assertion: Homogeneous horizontally-scaled nodes must be batched using Python lists to construct clean fan-out and fan-in data flow pipelines (e.g. lb >> [w1, w2, w3] >> db) without code redundancy or layout clutter.
Semantic isolation boundaries (tiers, regions, availability zones, microservices) must be modeled using Cluster context managers, with nesting achieved through Python block indentation.
